summary: Ruth W. Dunnell specializes in sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her PhD from Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi (1987–1988), and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College.
Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under doctoral supervisor Jason Neelis (attested 2017).

Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MA in Religious Studies from Naropa University, studying with numerous academic teachers including Judith Simmer-Brown, and studied under traditional teachers Tsultrim Allione, Gochen Tulku Sang-ngag Rinpoche, and Urgyen Wangchuk.

Ryan Richard Overbey works in Buddhist and religious studies, having studied at Brown University (AB 2001) and Harvard University (PhD 2010). His academic career includes appointments at Heidelberg Academy, Holy Cross, UC Berkeley, Wesleyan University, and Skidmore College.
Ryo Kuroiwa specializes in computational fields and Indology. Kuroiwa has held posts at the National Institute of Informatics and the Graduate University for Advanced Studies.
Ryo Nishimura (1972–2016) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1999) and under Fumihiko Sueki (~1999–2004).
Ryosho Taira (1906–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Taisho University, where he is attested in 1984 and was attested as professor emeritus in 1976.
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. Kudo has held posts as a full-time lecturer at Taisho University (attested 2015–2026) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara (1909–2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin under Ryotai Hatani, Ryujo Yamada, and Shun'ichi Takagi. He lectured at Humboldt University and served as professor at Ryukoku University (~1961–1978).
Ryoichi Kondo (1930–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryoji Kishino is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Kishino has served as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Ryojin Soga (1875–1971) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Otani University, Shinshu University, and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He was a Toyo University professor (1916–1924) and held professorships, emeritus status, and the presidency (1961–1967) at Otani University.

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Mitomo served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).

Ryokei Kaginushi (1926–2005) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He served as a professor in the Faculty of Letters (attested 1978) and later as professor (attested 1993) at Otani University.
Ryoken Nawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who has served as a commissioned researcher at Kyoto Koka Women's University (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Osaka University (attested 2020–2026).

Ryoko Mochizuki (born 1933) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Mochizuki studied at the University of Tokyo until 1963 and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1972 and 1983).

Ryosaburo Sakaki (1872–1946) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Karl Florenz and Alfred Foucher, later teaching at Ryukoku University, Third Higher School, and Kyoto University.

Ryosei Fukuda (born 1937) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed degrees at Toyo University. He held posts including professor (from 1973) and professor emeritus (from 2007) at Taisho University, visiting professor at Shuchiin University, and director at several Chisan institutions.

Ryoshin Nakao (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Komazawa University (~1971–1980) and held appointments as a professor at Hanazono University (~1995) and as a staff member at the Research Institute of Soto Studies.

Ryosho Hayashi (1927–2008) studied at Taisho University and Tokyo Metropolitan University in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He held appointments at Taisho University as professor (1975), Dean of Letters (1981), and professor emeritus (1990–1994).
